audit_findings.title: The valuation mixes a pre-acquisition earnings perimeter with a post-acquisition balance sheet
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.680m purchase price ($0.52/share), including $3.368m June 2026 contingent consideration ($0.09/share); owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge reflects cash spent after closing while the anchor excludes New Classic earnings; omitted acquired earnings understate value, while any unbridged earn-out, integration costs or liabilities overstate value.
audit_findings.evidence: As the transaction was completed subsequent to December 31, 2025, it is not reflected in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its net valuation effect is not. The known purchase price is only 0.86% of the $2,183m base equity value, while New Classic's sustainable owner earnings and integration requirements are not isolated. The record therefore cannot establish whether the mixed effects are material.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate owner earnings from the post-acquisition 10-Q, separately identifying New Classic earnings, working capital, integration costs and purchase-accounting effects; reconcile the $3.368m contingent consideration and all acquisition cash flows in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include funds owed to marketplace participants
audit_findings.magnitude: $65.173m filed at 2025-12-31; June 2026 amount unquantified; $65.173m equals $1.82/share and 17.2% of the $377.831m cash/STI bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Refundable participant deposits and seller collections are included in consolidated cash but represent offsetting claims; adding that cash without subtracting the claims inflates the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Receipts on GigaCloud Marketplace include (1) refundable deposits on GigaCloud Marketplace, representing the balance of deposits from Buyers and Sellers which could be withdrawn or used for their future purchase of the Group’s services or merchandise on GigaCloud Marketplace; and, (2) amounts payable to Sellers that the Group collects from Buyers in relation to the GigaCloud 3P services it provides on GigaCloud Marketplace.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence and prior-year amount of participant obligations are demonstrated, although the June amount is unresolved. If the prior-year amount remained, the $1.82/share adjustment would exceed the $1.52/share margin between the $53.27 bear value and the $51.75 price, so it is reasonably capable of changing the downside conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 breakdown of the $125.333m accrued expenses and other current liabilities, trace marketplace receipts to cash accounts, and rerun the bridge using cash net of refundable deposits, seller payables and required operating liquidity.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may omit an unrecorded repatriation-tax claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.0m disclosed at 2025-12-31, equal to $0.81/share, 7.7% of the cash/STI bridge and 1.3%-1.5% of scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Income and withholding taxes would reduce the portion of offshore cash assumed distributable to common shareholders if repatriated.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 , 2024 and 2023 respectively, the Group has not recorded approximately $ 29.0 million, $ 19.9 million and $ 12.5 million of deferred tax liabilities associated with remaining unremitted foreign earnings considered indefinitely reinvested, for which foreign income and withholding taxes would be due upon repatriation.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax exposure is disclosed, but payment is conditional on repatriation and is not a demonstrated present liability. Even deducting the full $29.0m would reduce bear value from $53.27 to about $52.46 and base value from $61.00 to about $60.19, leaving both above the $51.75 price and leaving the buy-below conclusion unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Map June cash and investments by jurisdiction and legal entity; rerun the bridge net of applicable taxes only for amounts assumed to require taxable repatriation.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require recurring working-capital investment absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $75.168m computed H1 2026 working-capital outflow, or $2.10/share and 58.5% of the $128.5m anchor; normalized recurring requirement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental inventory, receivables, prepayments and other operating capital consume cash needed to support forecast growth and should reduce forecast owner earnings or the growth rate.
audit_findings.evidence: Our business requires significant capital investments and a high level of working capital to sustain our operations and business growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial growth-related cash absorption: $19.247m from receivables, $22.743m from inventory, $22.058m from prepayments and other assets, $10.277m from payables and accrued liabilities, and $0.843m from contract liabilities. Timing and acquisition effects prevent treating all $75.168m as recurring, but its scale is sufficient to make the unmodeled normalized requirement material, particularly to the 3%-6% growth cases.
audit_findings.action: Build a post-New Classic normalized working-capital schedule using inventory turns, receivable days, supplier terms and prepayment requirements, then rerun each growth scenario after deducting the incremental investment required.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may retain non-recurring legal-related gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.510m gross FY2025 line; legal and other non-recurring portion unquantified; the gross line equals 3.5% of the $128.5m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any non-recurring legal receipt retained in anchor owner earnings is projected and capitalized as recurring operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Other gains, net was $4.5 million in 2025, primarily attributable to credit card cash back, payments to be received from or paid to legal claims and others.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the mixed line contains legal-claim amounts, but it does not identify their amount or establish how much entered the owner-earnings anchor. If the entire $4.510m were embedded, a proportional reduction would lower base operating PV by about $63.3m, or $1.77/share, before tax and normalization effects; the actual effect could be much smaller because credit-card cash back is recurring. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 ledger-level composition of the $4.510m line, identify recurring cash-back economics and net legal settlements, remove verified one-offs from the anchor, and rerun all scenarios.
